why: Each barter is one roll on the piglin_bartering loot table. Expected pearls per ingot = (pearl weight / total weight) x (mean stack size). In 1.16.1 the pearl entry has weight 20 of 423 and gives 4-8 pearls (mean 6): 0.2837 pearls per ingot. 32 ingots give 9.08 pearls on average; 12 pearls need 42.3 ingots on average.
trap: Using the other version's table (2.09 pearls, 183.6 ingots) or today's table (weight 10 of 469). Expected pearls per ingot fell about 4.3x in 1.16.2; Wikipedia gives the higher pearl rate as a reason 1.16-1.19 runs use 1.16.1.

techniques.description: Know the barter table of the version being run.

sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minecraft_speedrunning (raw line 41: 1.16.1 used because the pearl barter rate is higher)

alternates.why_valid: Rounded; rounding up to whole ingots is reasonable and within tolerance.

broken.why_wrong: Uses the other 1.16 version's barter table.
